answer: Persistent history pricing: each new identity pays a rising fee set by the prior count of active identities, so the oasis of cheap accounts dries up as the network grows, functioning as a cost beacon that makes honest participation the low-cost path. Reputation earned slowly then unlocks fee waivers, so a raven flock of clones must fund every fake at the marginal price plus the lost waiver value. An attacker cloning N identities pays the full escalating schedule with no amortization, while one honest agent pays once and accrues discounts.
